name: United States (24 stars, 1822–1836)
description: Thirteen alternating red and white stripes with a navy canton bearing twenty-four white five-pointed stars in four rows of six.
history: The 24-star flag became official on 4 July 1822 after the admission of Missouri and flew for fourteen years, the longest-serving design before the twentieth century. It was during this period, in 1831, that sea captain William Driver reportedly named his flag 'Old Glory'. It was replaced on 4 July 1836 by the 25-star flag for Arkansas.
